rationale: Jesus introduces the words with a citation formula, "Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator 'made them male and female'" (19:4, BSB), and the BSB sets them in quotation marks. Genesis 1:27 ends "male and female He created them" (BSB). The English verbs differ ("made" against "created"), but the Greek does not: all nine editions Bible Hub lists for Matthew 19:4 read arsen kai thely epoiesen autous, and Swete's Septuagint of Genesis 1:27 ends with the same four words. The formula and the verbatim Greek are why this is quotation and explicit, following conn-matt15-honor-exodus20. This row is separate from conn-gen2-marriage-matt19, which covers the Genesis 2:24 quotation in 19:5 and names this one only as lying outside its range. Genesis 5:2 ("He created them male and female," BSB) repeats the phrase; 19:4's "from the beginning" points to the creation account, so the row is drawn to 1:27. Mark 10:6 carries the same quotation.
